source.text: Δικαιωθέντες οὖν ἐκ πίστεως εἰρήνην ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ οὗ καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν τῇ πίστει εἰς τὴν χάριν ταύτην ἐν ᾗ ἑστήκαμεν, καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Having been justified therefore by faith peace we have toward the God through the Lord of us Jesus Christ, \v 2 through whom also the access we have had by the faith into the grace this in which we stand, and we boast on hope of the glory of the God;

en.L: Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 2 through whom we have also had access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we boast in hope of the glory of God.
en.B: So now that we have been declared righteous by faith, we are at peace with God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 2 Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have also been brought by faith into this grace where we now stand, and we boast in the hope of sharing God's glory.
en.R: God has made us right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} through faith. So now there is peace between God and us, through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 2 Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have come by faith into God's grace, and we stand firm in it. And we rejoice, because we have the hope of sharing in God's glory.

es.L: Así que, habiendo sido justificados por la fe, tenemos paz con Dios por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, \v 2 por medio de quien también hemos tenido acceso por la fe a esta gracia en la que nos mantenemos, y nos gloriamos con [la] esperanza de la gloria de Dios.
es.B: Así pues, ahora que hemos sido justificados por la fe, estamos en paz con Dios por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. \v 2 Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} también hemos sido llevados por la fe a esta gracia en la que ahora nos mantenemos, y nos gloriamos en la esperanza de participar de la gloria de Dios.
es.R: Dios nos ha declarado justos por medio de la fe. Por eso ahora hay paz entre Dios y nosotros, por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. \v 2 Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y por la fe, hemos entrado en la gracia de Dios, y en ella nos mantenemos firmes. Y nos alegramos, porque tenemos la esperanza de participar en la gloria de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, tukiwa tumehesabiwa haki kwa imani, tuna amani na Mungu kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, \v 2 ambaye kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} pia tumepata njia ya kuingia kwa imani katika neema hii ambamo tumesimama, na tunajivunia katika tumaini la utukufu wa Mungu.
sw.B: Basi, kwa kuwa sasa tumehesabiwa haki kwa imani, tuna amani na Mungu kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 2 Kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} pia tumeletwa kwa imani katika neema hii, ambamo sasa tumesimama, nasi tunajivunia tumaini la kushiriki utukufu wa Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu ametuhesabia haki kwa sababu ya imani. Kwa hiyo sasa kuna amani kati ya Mungu na sisi, kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 2 Kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, kwa imani, tumeingia katika neema ya Mungu, nasi tunasimama imara ndani yake. Tena tunafurahi, kwa sababu tuna tumaini la kushiriki utukufu wa Mungu.

fr.L: Ayant donc été justifiés par la foi, nous avons la paix avec Dieu par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, \v 2 par qui nous avons aussi eu accès par la foi à cette grâce dans laquelle nous nous tenons, et nous nous glorifions dans [l’]espérance de la gloire de Dieu.
fr.B: Maintenant donc que nous avons été justifiés par la foi, nous sommes en paix avec Dieu par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. \v 2 Par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, nous avons aussi été introduits par la foi dans cette grâce où nous nous tenons maintenant, et nous nous glorifions dans l’espérance d’avoir part à la gloire de Dieu.
fr.R: Dieu nous a déclarés justes par la foi. Alors maintenant, il y a la paix entre Dieu et nous, par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. \v 2 Par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, nous sommes entrés par la foi dans la grâce de Dieu, et nous y tenons bon. Et nous nous réjouissons, parce que nous avons l’espérance d’avoir part à la gloire de Dieu.

vi.L: Vậy, đã được xưng công chính bởi đức tin, chúng ta có bình an với Đức Chúa Trời qua Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, \v 2 nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chúng ta cũng đã được dẫn vào, bởi đức tin, trong ân điển này, là nơi chúng ta đang đứng vững, và chúng ta khoe mình trong niềm hy vọng về vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Vậy, vì đã được xưng công chính bởi đức tin, chúng ta có bình an với Đức Chúa Trời qua Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. \v 2 Nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, bởi đức tin, chúng ta cũng đã được đưa vào ân điển này, là nơi chúng ta hiện đang đứng vững, và chúng ta tự hào trong niềm hy vọng được dự phần vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã công nhận chúng ta là công chính qua đức tin. Vì vậy, giờ đây giữa Đức Chúa Trời và chúng ta có bình an, qua Chúa chúng ta, Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. \v 2 Nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, bởi đức tin chúng ta đã được vào trong ân điển của Đức Chúa Trời, và chúng ta đứng vững trong ân điển ấy. Chúng ta vui mừng vì có niềm hy vọng được dự phần vinh quang của Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러므로 우리는 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정받았으니, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통하여 하나님과 평화를 누리고 있습니다. \v 2 우리는 그분을 통하여 믿음으로 우리가 서 있는 이 은혜에 들어감도 얻었고, 하나님의 영광에 대한 소망 안에서 자랑합니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 우리는 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정받았으니, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통해 하나님과 평화를 누립니다. \v 2 또 우리는 그분을 통해 믿음으로 지금 서 있는 이 은혜 안으로 들어오게 되었고, 하나님의 영광에 참여할 소망을 자랑합니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 믿음을 통해 우리를 의롭다고 인정해 주셨습니다. 그래서 이제 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통해 하나님과 우리 사이에 평화가 있습니다. \v 2 우리는 그분을 통해 믿음으로 하나님의 은혜 안에 들어왔고, 그 은혜 안에 굳게 서 있습니다. 그리고 우리는 하나님의 영광을 함께 누리게 될 소망이 있기 때문에 기뻐합니다.

decisions.choice: "we have peace": a statement
alternatives: "let us have peace with God" (an encouragement)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the indicative, "we have". Many early and important manuscripts read the subjunctive, "let us have peace", which differs by one vowel; the two sounded alike when read aloud, so copyists easily confused them. The statement fits the argument: Paul is describing what God has done for those declared righteous, and verses 2-11 go on in statements. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: peace with God: the end of hostility between God and people
decisions.reason: The peace is not first a feeling of calm but a changed relationship: those who were God's enemies (verse 10) are now reconciled to him. It is the peace of the Hebrew shalom, wholeness and well-being given by God.

decisions.choice: therefore: drawing the conclusion of chapters 3-4
decisions.reason: "Having been justified by faith" gathers up what Paul has shown in 3:21-4:25, that God declares righteous those who believe, as he did Abraham. Chapter 5 now says what follows from it.

decisions.choice: access: being brought into the presence of a king or of God
decisions.reason: prosagōgē is the right of approach, the way in to someone of high rank. Paul uses it in Ephesians 2:18 and 3:12 of coming to the Father. The perfect "we have had" means the access was given and remains.

decisions.choice: "by faith" stands in the text
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts leave out "by faith" in verse 2, and others read "in faith". The SBLGNT keeps "by faith". The meaning is the same either way, since verse 1 has already said it. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: boast: glory in, take proud confidence in
decisions.reason: kauchaomai is to boast or to glory in something. In 2:17, 2:23 and 3:27 Paul rejected boasting in the law and in one's own works; here the believer's boasting rests on what God will do, as in Jeremiah 9:23-24, "let the one who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me" (Jeremiah 9:22-23 in the Hebrew numbering).

decisions.choice: the hope of the glory of God: hope of sharing God's glory
decisions.reason: In 3:23 all "fall short of the glory of God". The hope here is that believers will share that glory when God completes their salvation (8:17-18, 8:21, 8:30).

decisions.choice: declared righteous (B); made right with God (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:13, 3:24 and 4:2: Literal keeps "justified", Balanced says what the word means in a court, and Readable says what it means for the person, made right with God.

decisions.choice: the hope of sharing (in) God's glory
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the hope is, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: rejoice
decisions.reason: To a young reader, "boast" sounds like showing off. Readable says "rejoice" for this boasting in what God does, here and in verses 3 and 11; Literal and Balanced keep "boast", so that the link with 2:17-23 and 3:27 can be seen.

decisions.choice: nos gloriamos (L, B); nos alegramos (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as glad, confident pride. "Gloriarse" (as 2:17 and 2:23 have for boasting in God and in the law) carries that without the arrogance of "jactarse", which the letter keeps for wrong boasting (3:27, 11:18). Readable says "alegrarse", as the English Readable says "rejoice". The same choice holds in verses 3 and 11.

decisions.choice: Dios nos ha declarado justos
alternatives: Dios nos ha puesto en una relación correcta con él
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "made us right with himself", Spanish Readable says "declarar justo" for the verb, as settled at 2:13 and used at 3:24.

decisions.choice: tunajivunia (L, B); tunafurahi (R)
decisions.reason: "Kujivunia" is the word 2:17 and 2:23 use for boasting in God and in the law; with an object worth trusting it is proud confidence, which is the sense the meaning decision gives. "Kujivuna" (3:27) is conceit and would be wrong here. Readable says "kufurahi", as the English Readable says "rejoice". The same choice holds in verses 3 and 11.

decisions.choice: Mungu ametuhesabia haki
alternatives: Mungu ametuweka katika uhusiano mwema naye
decisions.reason: As settled at 2:13, "kuhesabiwa haki" is kept at every level; Readable makes God the subject, as at 3:24, where the English Readable says "made us right with himself".

decisions.choice: "justifiés" (L, B); "déclarés justes" (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As settled at 2:13: Literal and Balanced keep the traditional verb "justifier", and Readable says "déclarer juste", God’s verdict that the word describes. "Rendre juste" would suggest a change of character rather than a verdict. The noun "la justice" stays the same at every level, as a key term.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Romans is a letter, not a narrative: Paul speaks to his readers about what God has done for them, and French uses the passé composé for that, as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: "Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" (L), "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" (B, R); "{{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" where the Greek has no article, "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" where French needs one outside the span; "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ" (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians and Hebrews. French says "Christ" without an article but "le Messie" with one, so where the Greek has no article the article goes inside the span; where French needs the article anyway (after a preposition or with "du") it stays outside, since both options read naturally.

decisions.choice: "nous nous glorifions" (L, B); "nous nous réjouissons" (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Se vanter" says bragging in French, which is not Paul's point here. "Se glorifier de" is the usual French for proud confidence in something and keeps the link with the boasting Paul rejected in 2:17, 2:23 and 3:27. Readable says "se réjouir", as the English Readable says "rejoice".

decisions.choice: "l'espérance" at every level (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "L'espoir" is a wish that may fail; "l'espérance" is confident expectation, the hope Paul says does not disappoint (verse 5). It is still an ordinary French word, so Readable keeps it.

decisions.choice: "khoe mình" (L); "tự hào" (B); "vui mừng" (R) in this chapter (verses 2, 3 and 11)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "khoe mình", the word for this family through the letter (2:17, 3:27, 4:2). Here the boasting is proud confidence in what God gives (m6), so Balanced says "tự hào", as in 2:17, not the "khoe khoang" of 3:27. Readable says "vui mừng", as the English Readable says "rejoice".

decisions.choice: "có bình an với Đức Chúa Trời" at every level
alternatives: "được hòa thuận với Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: "Bình an" is the key term for peace, kept at every level. The meaning decision reads this as peace between God and people after hostility, which "bình an với" says, and verse 10 then names the reconciliation.

decisions.choice: "đã được dẫn vào" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek noun is the access of one brought into a king's presence (m4). Vietnamese says it with the verb "được dẫn vào", which keeps the picture without a bracketed noun.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 with "여러분" and "우리"; {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}; "의롭다고 인정하다"; no deity_pronoun spans (as through the letter)
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:1 and 2:13: the letter is in 합쇼체 at every level, the christos alternative is plain "메시아", God's verdict is "의롭다고 인정하다" at every level, and Korean has no deity_pronoun spans because it has no capital letters for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "하나님과 평화" for peace with God
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says this peace is first a changed relationship, the end of hostility between God and people (verse 10). Korean "평화" is the word for peace between parties, as in Colossians 1:20 and Romans 3:17; "평안", the key-term word, is kept for the peace God gives in greetings and blessings (1:7, 2:10). "화평" is older church language.

decisions.choice: "자랑하다" (L, B); "기뻐하다" (R), here and in verses 3 and 11
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "자랑하다", the word for this family through the letter (2:17), so the reader can see that the boasting Paul rejected in 2:17-3:27 is now replaced by boasting in what God does (meaning decision). Readable says "기뻐하다", as the English Readable says "rejoice".

source.text: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν, εἰδότες ὅτι ἡ θλῖψις ὑπομονὴν κατεργάζεται, ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ δοκιμήν, ἡ δὲ δοκιμὴ ἐλπίδα.

records.literal_gloss: Not only and, but also we boast in the troubles, knowing that the trouble endurance produces, \v 4 the and endurance proven character, the and proven character hope.

en.L: And not only [that], but we also boast in the troubles, knowing that trouble produces endurance, \v 4 and endurance, proven character, and proven character, hope.
en.B: More than that, we boast even in our troubles, because we know that trouble leads to endurance, \v 4 endurance to proven character, and proven character to hope.
en.R: And that is not all. We rejoice even when we have troubles. We know that troubles teach us to keep going. \v 4 When we keep going, we are tested and shown to be genuine. And that gives us hope.

es.L: Y no solo [eso], sino que también nos gloriamos en las aflicciones, sabiendo que la aflicción produce perseverancia, \v 4 y la perseverancia, carácter probado, y el carácter probado, esperanza.
es.B: Más aún, nos gloriamos incluso en nuestras aflicciones, porque sabemos que la aflicción lleva a la perseverancia, \v 4 la perseverancia a un carácter probado, y el carácter probado a la esperanza.
es.R: Y eso no es todo. Nos alegramos aun cuando pasamos por dificultades. Sabemos que las dificultades nos enseñan a seguir adelante. \v 4 Cuando seguimos adelante, somos puestos a prueba y se ve que somos auténticos. Y eso nos da esperanza.

sw.L: Na si [hilo] tu, bali pia tunajivunia katika dhiki, tukijua kwamba dhiki huleta uvumilivu, \v 4 na uvumilivu, tabia iliyothibitika, na tabia iliyothibitika, tumaini.
sw.B: Zaidi ya hayo, tunajivunia hata katika dhiki zetu, kwa sababu tunajua kwamba dhiki huleta uvumilivu, \v 4 uvumilivu huleta tabia iliyojaribiwa na kuthibitika, na tabia hiyo huleta tumaini.
sw.R: Na si hayo tu. Tunafurahi hata tunapopatwa na taabu. Tunajua kwamba taabu hutufundisha kuvumilia. \v 4 Tunapovumilia, tunajaribiwa na kuonekana kuwa wa kweli. Na hilo linatupa tumaini.

fr.L: Et non seulement [cela], mais nous nous glorifions aussi dans les détresses, sachant que la détresse produit l’endurance, \v 4 et l’endurance, un caractère éprouvé, et le caractère éprouvé, l’espérance.
fr.B: Bien plus, nous nous glorifions même dans nos détresses, car nous savons que la détresse mène à l’endurance, \v 4 l’endurance à un caractère éprouvé, et le caractère éprouvé à l’espérance.
fr.R: Et ce n’est pas tout. Nous nous réjouissons même quand nous avons des difficultés. Nous savons que les difficultés nous apprennent à tenir bon. \v 4 Quand nous tenons bon, nous sommes mis à l’épreuve, et nous en sortons solides. Et cela nous donne de l’espérance.

vi.L: Không những thế, nhưng chúng ta cũng khoe mình trong những hoạn nạn, vì biết rằng hoạn nạn sinh ra sự kiên trì, \v 4 sự kiên trì [sinh ra] phẩm chất đã qua thử thách, và phẩm chất đã qua thử thách [sinh ra] niềm hy vọng.
vi.B: Hơn thế nữa, chúng ta còn tự hào ngay cả trong hoạn nạn, vì biết rằng hoạn nạn đem lại sự kiên trì, \v 4 sự kiên trì đem lại phẩm chất được tôi luyện, và phẩm chất được tôi luyện đem lại niềm hy vọng.
vi.R: Không chỉ vậy. Chúng ta vui mừng ngay cả khi gặp khó khăn. Chúng ta biết rằng khó khăn dạy chúng ta bền lòng. \v 4 Khi chúng ta bền lòng, chúng ta được thử thách và cho thấy mình là thật. Điều đó đem lại cho chúng ta niềm hy vọng.

ko.L: 그뿐 아니라, 우리는 환난 가운데서도 자랑합니다. 환난은 인내를 낳고, \v 4 인내는 검증된 성품을, 검증된 성품은 소망을 [낳는다는] 것을 알기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그뿐 아니라, 우리는 환난 중에도 자랑합니다. 환난이 인내로 이어지고, \v 4 인내가 검증된 성품으로, 검증된 성품이 소망으로 이어진다는 것을 우리가 알기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그것만이 아닙니다. 우리는 어려움을 당할 때에도 기뻐합니다. 어려움은 우리에게 끝까지 견디는 법을 가르쳐 준다는 것을 알기 때문입니다. \v 4 끝까지 견디면, 우리는 시험을 거쳐 참된 사람으로 인정받습니다. 그리고 그것이 우리에게 소망을 줍니다.

decisions.choice: troubles: hardship and pressure of every kind
decisions.reason: thlipsis is pressure, distress, affliction. Paul uses it of the hardships believers suffer for their faith and in a fallen world (8:35, 2 Corinthians 4:17), and in 2:9 of the distress that comes on evildoers.

decisions.choice: endurance: holding out under pressure
decisions.reason: hypomonē is staying under a load without giving way: steadfast, patient endurance, not mere waiting (2:7, 8:25, 15:4).

decisions.choice: proven character: the quality of having been tested and found genuine
decisions.reason: dokimē is the result of a test, the approval of something that has stood it, like metal tried in the fire (2 Corinthians 2:9, 8:2, Philippians 2:22). Endurance in trouble shows that a person's faith is real.

decisions.choice: not only that: the boasting of verse 2 goes further
decisions.reason: The short phrase refers back to verse 2: believers boast not only in the hope of glory but even in present troubles, because of what the troubles produce.

decisions.choice: rejoice
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the chain of three steps
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb in the second and third steps. Balanced lets "leads to" carry over; Readable spells the steps out in short sentences.

decisions.choice: aflicción; perseverancia
decisions.reason: The words already settled in Romans: "aflicción" for trouble (2:9, 12:12) and "perseverancia" for endurance (2:7, 15:4). "Paciencia" would suggest calm waiting rather than holding out under pressure, which is the sense the meaning decision gives.

decisions.choice: carácter probado
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision: the quality of having been tested and found genuine. "Prueba" alone would sound like the test rather than its result.

decisions.choice: dhiki; uvumilivu
decisions.reason: The words already settled in Romans: "dhiki" for trouble (2:9, 12:12) and "uvumilivu" for endurance (15:4). Readable says "taabu" and "kuvumilia", the everyday words.

decisions.choice: tabia iliyothibitika (L); tabia iliyojaribiwa na kuthibitika (B)
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision: character that has been tested and shown to be genuine. Balanced names both the testing and the result.

decisions.choice: "la détresse" (L, B); "les difficultés" (R)
decisions.reason: "Tribulation" is church language, and "épreuve" would blur the word with the testing of verse 4 ("caractère éprouvé"). "Détresse" says the pressure and distress of the Greek word.

decisions.choice: "hoạn nạn", "sự kiên trì", "phẩm chất đã qua thử thách" (L) / "phẩm chất được tôi luyện" (B)
decisions.reason: "Hoạn nạn" is hardship and pressure of every kind (m1). "Kiên trì" is holding out under pressure (m2), as in 2:7; "nhịn nhục" is kept for God's patience (2:4). The third word is character that has been tested and found genuine (m3): Literal says so, and Balanced uses the picture of metal refined in fire. "Từng trải" is the older wording and now means simply "experienced".

decisions.choice: "환난" (L, B) / "어려움" (R); "검증된 성품" (L, B) for proven character
decisions.reason: "환난" is the word used for this noun in 2:9 and in the Korean of John and Colossians. For the result of a test the meaning decision describes, "검증된 성품" says plainly that character has been tested and found genuine; "연단" is older church language that many readers no longer understand.

source.text: ἡ δὲ ἐλπὶς οὐ καταισχύνει· ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου τοῦ δοθέντος ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: The and hope not puts to shame, because the love of the God has been poured out in the hearts of us through Spirit Holy the [one] having been given to us.

en.L: And hope does not put [us] to shame, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through [the] Holy Spirit who was given to us.
en.B: And hope does not leave us ashamed, for God has given us the Holy Spirit, and through the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love has flooded our hearts.
en.R: This hope will never let us down. God has filled our hearts with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love by giving us the Holy Spirit.

es.L: Y la esperanza no [nos] avergüenza, porque el amor de Dios se ha derramado en nuestros corazones por medio del Espíritu Santo, que se nos dio.
es.B: Y la esperanza no nos deja avergonzados, pues Dios nos ha dado el Espíritu Santo, y por medio del Espíritu {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor ha inundado nuestros corazones.
es.R: Esta esperanza nunca nos va a defraudar. Dios ha llenado nuestros corazones con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor al darnos el Espíritu Santo.

sw.L: Na tumaini halituaibishi, kwa sababu upendo wa Mungu umemiminwa ndani ya mioyo yetu kupitia Roho Mtakatifu aliyetolewa kwetu.
sw.B: Na tumaini hili halituachi na aibu, kwa maana Mungu ametupa Roho Mtakatifu, na kupitia Roho upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} umejaa tele mioyoni mwetu.
sw.R: Tumaini hili halitatuangusha kamwe. Mungu ameijaza mioyo yetu upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa kutupa Roho Mtakatifu.

fr.L: Et l’espérance ne [nous] couvre pas de honte, parce que l’amour de Dieu a été répandu dans nos cœurs par [l’]Esprit Saint qui nous a été donné.
fr.B: Et l’espérance ne nous laisse pas dans la honte, car Dieu nous a donné l’Esprit Saint, et par l’Esprit, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour a inondé nos cœurs.
fr.R: Cette espérance ne nous décevra jamais. Dieu a rempli nos cœurs de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour en nous donnant l’Esprit Saint.

vi.L: Và niềm hy vọng không làm [chúng ta] hổ thẹn, vì tình yêu thương của Đức Chúa Trời đã được đổ ra trong lòng chúng ta bởi Đức Thánh Linh, là Đấng đã được ban cho chúng ta.
vi.B: Niềm hy vọng ấy không để chúng ta phải hổ thẹn, vì Đức Chúa Trời đã ban Đức Thánh Linh cho chúng ta, và qua Thánh Linh, tình yêu thương của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã tràn ngập lòng chúng ta.
vi.R: Niềm hy vọng này sẽ không bao giờ làm chúng ta thất vọng. Đức Chúa Trời đã ban Đức Thánh Linh cho chúng ta, và qua đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đổ đầy tình yêu thương của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào lòng chúng ta.

ko.L: 그리고 소망은 [우리를] 부끄럽게 하지 않습니다. 하나님의 사랑이 우리에게 주신 성령을 통하여 우리 마음에 부어졌기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 이 소망은 우리를 부끄럽게 하지 않습니다. 하나님께서 우리에게 성령을 주셨고, 성령을 통해 그분의 사랑이 우리 마음에 넘치도록 부어졌기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 이 소망은 결코 우리를 실망시키지 않습니다. 하나님께서 우리에게 성령을 주셔서, 우리 마음을 그분의 사랑으로 가득 채워 주셨기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: hope that does not end in shame: Psalm 22:6 and 25:20
decisions.reason: In the Psalms, those who trust in God "are not put to shame" (Psalm 22:6, 25:20 in the Hebrew numbering; Isaiah 28:16, quoted in 9:33 and 10:11). To be put to shame is to have one's hope fail before everyone, above all at God's judgment. The hope of believers will not fail them.

decisions.choice: the love of God: God's love for us
decisions.reason: The phrase could mean our love for God, but verse 8 speaks of God's love for us, shown in Christ's death, and the hope rests on that love, not on ours.

decisions.choice: poured out: given richly
decisions.reason: The verb recalls the promise that God would pour out his Spirit (Joel 3:1-2 in the Hebrew numbering, Acts 2:17-18, 2:33). The perfect tense says the love was poured out and is still there.

decisions.choice: who was given: a single past gift
decisions.reason: The aorist points to the time believers received the Spirit when they came to faith (8:9, Galatians 3:2).

decisions.choice: has flooded (B); has filled (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "poured out" pictures: God's love given in full measure. Both make God the giver of the Spirit, as the passive "who was given" implies, and Balanced repeats "the Spirit" rather than use a pronoun.

decisions.choice: will never let us down
decisions.reason: Readable puts "put to shame" in everyday words: the hope will not turn out to be false.

decisions.choice: no [nos] avergüenza
decisions.reason: Spanish "avergonzar" needs an object; Literal supplies it in brackets, as the English Literal does with "[us]".

decisions.choice: "niềm hy vọng" at every level (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Niềm hy vọng" is the plain modern word for confident hope and is kept at every level, as in the Vietnamese Colossians (1:5). "Sự trông cậy" is the older church word and now sounds like reliance on someone.

decisions.choice: "부어졌다" (L); "넘치도록 부어졌다" (B); "가득 채워 주셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb recalls the promise that God would pour out his Spirit (meaning decision). Literal keeps "부어지다"; Balanced keeps the picture and adds the fullness it means; Readable says it plainly.

source.text: Ἔτι γὰρ Χριστὸς ὄντων ἡμῶν ἀσθενῶν ἔτι κατὰ καιρὸν ὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν ἀπέθανεν.

records.literal_gloss: Still for Christ, being us weak, still according to time on behalf of ungodly died.

en.L: For while we were still weak, yet at the right time, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} died for [the] ungodly.
en.B: While we were still helpless, at the time God had chosen, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for the ungodly.
en.R: We had no strength to save ourselves. But when the time that God chose had come, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for us, even though we did not honor God.

es.L: Porque cuando todavía éramos débiles, aun así, en el momento señalado, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió por [los] impíos.
es.B: Cuando todavía no teníamos fuerzas, en el tiempo que Dios había escogido, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió por los impíos.
es.R: No teníamos fuerzas para salvarnos a nosotros mismos. Pero cuando llegó el tiempo que Dios había escogido, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió por nosotros, aunque no honrábamos a Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana tulipokuwa bado dhaifu, hata hivyo kwa wakati unaofaa, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa kwa ajili ya wasiomcha Mungu.
sw.B: Tulipokuwa bado hatuna nguvu, kwa wakati ambao Mungu alikuwa ameuchagua, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa kwa ajili ya wasiomcha Mungu.
sw.R: Hatukuwa na nguvu za kujiokoa wenyewe. Lakini wakati ambao Mungu aliuchagua ulipofika, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa kwa ajili yetu, ingawa hatukumheshimu Mungu.

fr.L: Car, alors que nous étions encore faibles, au moment voulu, {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est mort pour [des] impies.
fr.B: Alors que nous étions encore sans force, au temps que Dieu avait choisi, {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est mort pour les impies.
fr.R: Nous n’avions pas la force de nous sauver nous-mêmes. Mais quand le moment choisi par Dieu est arrivé, {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est mort pour nous, alors que nous n’honorions pas Dieu.

vi.L: Vì khi chúng ta còn yếu đuối, đúng thời điểm, {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết vì những người không tin kính.
vi.B: Khi chúng ta còn bất lực, vào đúng thời điểm Đức Chúa Trời đã định, {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết vì những người không tin kính.
vi.R: Chúng ta không có sức tự cứu mình. Nhưng khi đến thời điểm Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn, {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết cho chúng ta, dù chúng ta không tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 우리가 아직 약할 때에, 바로 정한 때에, 경건하지 않은 사람들을 위하여 죽으셨습니다.
ko.B: 우리가 아직 무력할 때에, 하나님께서 정하신 때에 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 경건하지 않은 사람들을 위해 죽으셨습니다.
ko.R: 우리에게는 스스로를 구원할 힘이 없었습니다. 그러나 하나님께서 정하신 때가 되었을 때, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 우리를 위해 죽으셨습니다. 우리가 하나님을 공경하지 않았는데도 그렇게 하셨습니다.

decisions.choice: weak: without strength to save ourselves
decisions.reason: asthenēs is weak or sick. Here it describes people unable to do anything about their sin and their standing before God. Verses 8 and 10 say the same people were "sinners" and "enemies".

decisions.choice: at the right time: the time God set
decisions.reason: "According to time" means at the appointed or fitting moment, as in Galatians 4:4, "when the fullness of time came". The time was God's choice.

decisions.choice: "still" twice
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has "still" both at the start and before "at the right time". The second repeats and strengthens the first; some manuscripts smooth the sentence by changing or dropping one of them. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: for the ungodly: on behalf of people who did not honor God
decisions.reason: hyper is "on behalf of, for the sake of". The ungodly are the same "we": in 4:5 God "justifies the ungodly".

decisions.choice: the time God had chosen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose time it was, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: no strength to save ourselves; for us, even though we did not honor God
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of weakness is meant and that the ungodly are "us", as verses 8 and 10 make clear.

decisions.choice: wasiomcha Mungu
decisions.reason: "Ungodly" is said with the phrase 1:18 uses for ungodliness ("kutomcha Mungu"): people who do not fear or honour God. "Waovu" (the wicked) would lose the reference to God.

decisions.choice: "impies"
decisions.reason: "Impie" is the exact word for someone who does not honor God, and it keeps the link with 4:5, where God "justifies the ungodly". Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "아직 ... 바로 정한 때에" (L): the second "still" as "바로"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the second "still" repeats and strengthens the first. Korean "아직" twice would read as an error, so Literal gives the second its force with "바로"; "경건하지 않은" keeps the word of 4:5.

source.text: μόλις γὰρ ὑπὲρ δικαίου τις ἀποθανεῖται· ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ τάχα τις καὶ τολμᾷ ἀποθανεῖν·

records.literal_gloss: Scarcely for on behalf of righteous [one] someone will die; on behalf of for the good [one] perhaps someone even dares to die;

en.L: For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous [person]; for perhaps for the good [person] someone might even dare to die.
en.B: It is rare for anyone to give their life even for a righteous person; for a good person, perhaps, someone might find the courage to die.
en.R: It is rare for someone to die even for a person who does what is right. Someone might perhaps be brave enough to die for a person who is good and kind.

es.L: Porque difícilmente alguien morirá por un justo; pues quizá por el bueno alguno incluso se atrevería a morir.
es.B: Es raro que alguien dé su vida aun por una persona justa; por una persona buena, quizá, alguien llegue a tener el valor de morir.
es.R: Es raro que alguien muera aun por una persona que hace lo correcto. Quizá alguien sea lo bastante valiente para morir por una persona buena y generosa.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa shida mtu atakufa kwa ajili ya mwenye haki; kwa maana labda kwa ajili ya [mtu] mwema mtu fulani angethubutu hata kufa.
sw.B: Ni nadra mtu kutoa uhai wake hata kwa ajili ya mtu mwenye haki; kwa ajili ya mtu mwema, labda, mtu anaweza kupata ujasiri wa kufa.
sw.R: Ni nadra mtu kufa hata kwa ajili ya mtu anayetenda yaliyo sawa. Huenda mtu akawa na ujasiri wa kufa kwa ajili ya mtu mwema na mkarimu.

fr.L: Car à peine quelqu’un mourra-t-il pour un juste ; car pour [celui qui est] bon, peut-être quelqu’un ose-t-il même mourir.
fr.B: Il est rare qu’on donne sa vie, même pour un juste ; pour quelqu’un de bon, peut-être, on trouverait le courage de mourir.
fr.R: Il est rare que quelqu’un meure, même pour une personne qui fait ce qui est juste. Peut-être que quelqu’un aurait le courage de mourir pour une personne bonne et généreuse.

vi.L: Vì khó có ai chịu chết vì một người công chính; vì có lẽ vì một người tốt thì cũng có người dám chết.
vi.B: Hiếm có ai chịu hy sinh mạng sống mình ngay cả vì một người công chính; còn vì một người tốt, có lẽ cũng có người dám chết.
vi.R: Hiếm có ai chịu chết ngay cả cho một người công chính. Có lẽ cũng có người can đảm dám chết cho một người tốt bụng và tử tế.

ko.L: 의로운 사람을 위해서도 누가 죽는 일은 드뭅니다. 선한 사람을 위해서는 혹시 누가 감히 죽기까지 할지도 모릅니다.
ko.B: 의로운 사람을 위해서라도 자기 목숨을 내놓는 사람은 드뭅니다. 선한 사람을 위해서라면 혹시 용기를 내어 죽는 사람이 있을지도 모릅니다.
ko.R: 바르게 사는 사람을 위해서라도 대신 죽는 사람은 거의 없습니다. 착하고 친절한 사람을 위해서라면 혹시 용기를 내어 죽는 사람이 있을지도 모릅니다.

decisions.choice: righteous and good: an upright person and a generous benefactor
alternatives: the two words mean almost the same, and the second sentence corrects the first
"the good" as a thing: someone may dare to die for a good cause
decisions.reason: Paul sets two kinds of people side by side. The righteous person is just and upright; "the good" person (with the article) is most likely someone kind and generous, perhaps one's own benefactor, for whom gratitude might move someone to die. Either way, dying for anyone is rare, and Christ died for the ungodly.

decisions.choice: might even dare: a rare possibility
decisions.reason: "Perhaps" and "even dares" mark it as an exception: a few have been brave enough to die for a good person.

decisions.choice: give their life
decisions.reason: "Their" refers back to "anyone", as in everyday speech, and keeps the sentence for men and women alike.

decisions.choice: good and kind
decisions.reason: Readable shows the difference between the two people, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: buena y generosa
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes the good person as a generous benefactor; "generosa" says that where the English Readable says "good and kind".

decisions.choice: "on", "quelqu'un de bon"
decisions.reason: French "on" and "quelqu'un" already speak of anyone, man or woman, so no gender span is needed where the English Balanced needs "their".

decisions.choice: "người công chính" (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "a person who does what is right". "Công chính" is plain enough in Vietnamese, and keeping it lets the reader see the link with the key term of the letter.

decisions.choice: "자기 목숨을 내놓는 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "자기" and "사람" already speak of anyone, man or woman, so no gender span is needed where the English Balanced needs "their".

source.text: συνίστησιν δὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀγάπην εἰς ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ὄντων ἡμῶν Χριστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν.

records.literal_gloss: Shows but the of himself love toward us the God, that still sinners being us Christ on behalf of us died.

en.L: But God shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own love for us in that while we were still sinners, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} died for us.
en.B: But God proves how much {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves us: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for us when we were still sinners.
en.R: But God shows us how much {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves us. We were still sinners, and yet {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for us.

es.L: Pero Dios demuestra {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio amor por nosotros en esto: cuando todavía éramos pecadores, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió por nosotros.
es.B: Pero Dios prueba cuánto nos ama: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió por nosotros cuando todavía éramos pecadores.
es.R: Pero Dios nos muestra cuánto nos ama. Todavía éramos pecadores, y aun así {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió por nosotros.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu anaonyesha upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wenyewe kwetu, kwa kuwa tulipokuwa bado wenye dhambi, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa kwa ajili yetu.
sw.B: Lakini Mungu anathibitisha jinsi anavyotupenda: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa kwa ajili yetu tulipokuwa bado wenye dhambi.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu anatuonyesha jinsi anavyotupenda sana. Tulikuwa bado wenye dhambi, na hata hivyo {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikufa kwa ajili yetu.

fr.L: Mais Dieu démontre {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre amour envers nous en ce que, alors que nous étions encore pécheurs, {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est mort pour nous.
fr.B: Mais Dieu prouve combien {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous aime : {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est mort pour nous alors que nous étions encore pécheurs.
fr.R: Mais Dieu nous montre combien {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous aime. Nous étions encore pécheurs, et pourtant {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est mort pour nous.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời chứng tỏ tình yêu thương của chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đối với chúng ta ở chỗ khi chúng ta còn là tội nhân, {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết vì chúng ta.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời chứng tỏ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu thương chúng ta biết bao: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết vì chúng ta khi chúng ta còn là tội nhân.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời cho chúng ta thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu chúng ta biết bao. Chúng ta vẫn còn là tội nhân, vậy mà {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã chết cho chúng ta.

ko.L: 그러나 하나님께서는 우리가 아직 죄인이었을 때에 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 우리를 위하여 죽으심으로써, 우리를 향한 그분 자신의 사랑을 보여 주십니다.
ko.B: 그러나 하나님께서는 우리를 얼마나 사랑하시는지 확실히 보여 주십니다. 우리가 아직 죄인이었을 때 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 우리를 위해 죽으셨습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 하나님께서는 우리를 얼마나 사랑하시는지 우리에게 보여 주십니다. 우리는 아직 죄인이었지만, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 우리를 위해 죽으셨습니다.

decisions.choice: shows: proves, gives evidence
decisions.reason: synistēmi here is to show clearly or demonstrate, as in 3:5. The present tense means the cross keeps showing God's love.

decisions.choice: God's love is shown in Christ's death
decisions.reason: Paul says God shows his own love through Christ's death, so Christ's dying is God's own act of love, not an act that wins God over (8:32, 2 Corinthians 5:19).

decisions.choice: while we were still sinners
decisions.reason: The love came before any change in us: Christ died for people still in their sins, as verse 6 has said.

decisions.choice: proves how much he loves us
alternatives: shows his own love for us
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "his own love" into a clause and lets the colon do the work of "in that".

source.text: πολλῷ οὖν μᾶλλον δικαιωθέντες νῦν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ σωθησόμεθα δι’ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς.

records.literal_gloss: By much therefore more, having been justified now by the blood of him, we will be saved through him from the wrath.

en.L: Much more then, having now been justified by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, we will be saved through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the wrath.
en.B: Since we have now been declared righteous by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, it is all the more certain that we will be saved through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from God's wrath.
en.R: We have now been made right with God because {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} shed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood for us. So we can be even more sure that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save us from God's anger.

es.L: Mucho más, pues, habiendo sido ahora justificados por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre, seremos salvos por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de la ira.
es.B: Ya que ahora hemos sido justificados por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre, es todavía más seguro que por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} seremos salvos de la ira de Dios.
es.R: Ahora Dios nos ha declarado justos porque {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} derramó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre por nosotros. Así que podemos estar aún más seguros de que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos salvará de la ira de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, zaidi sana, kwa kuwa sasa tumehesabiwa haki kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, tutaokolewa kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kutoka katika ghadhabu.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa sasa tumehesabiwa haki kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ni hakika zaidi kwamba tutaokolewa kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kutoka katika ghadhabu ya Mungu.
sw.R: Sasa Mungu ametuhesabia haki kwa sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alimwaga damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa ajili yetu. Kwa hiyo tunaweza kuwa na uhakika zaidi kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atatuokoa kutoka katika hasira ya Mungu.

fr.L: Bien plus donc, maintenant justifiés par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang, nous serons sauvés par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de la colère.
fr.B: Puisque nous avons maintenant été justifiés par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang, il est d’autant plus certain que nous serons sauvés par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de la colère de Dieu.
fr.R: Maintenant, Dieu nous a déclarés justes, parce que {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a versé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang pour nous. Alors nous pouvons être encore plus sûrs qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous sauvera de la colère de Dieu.

vi.L: Huống chi bây giờ, đã được xưng công chính bởi huyết của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, chúng ta sẽ nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà được cứu khỏi cơn thịnh nộ.
vi.B: Vì bây giờ chúng ta đã được xưng công chính bởi huyết của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì chắc chắn hơn nữa chúng ta sẽ nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà được cứu khỏi cơn thịnh nộ của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Bây giờ chúng ta đã được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính vì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã đổ máu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho chúng ta. Vậy chúng ta càng có thể chắc chắn hơn rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ cứu chúng ta khỏi cơn giận của Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러므로 이제 우리가 그분의 피로 의롭다고 인정받았으니, 더욱더 그분을 통하여 진노에서 구원받을 것입니다.
ko.B: 이제 우리는 그분의 피로 의롭다고 인정받았으니, 그분을 통해 하나님의 진노에서 구원받을 것은 더욱 확실합니다.
ko.R: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 우리를 위해 피를 흘리셨기 때문에, 이제 우리는 하나님께 의롭다고 인정받았습니다. 그러니 그분이 하나님의 진노에서 우리를 구원하실 것을 더욱 확신할 수 있습니다.

decisions.choice: his blood: Christ's death as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: "Blood" stands for Christ's death, and recalls the blood of sacrifices (3:25). "By" gives the means: his death is how God declared us righteous.

decisions.choice: the wrath: God's judgment to come
decisions.reason: "The wrath" is God's coming judgment against sin (1:18, 2:5, 2:8, 1 Thessalonians 1:10). The future "we will be saved" looks to that day.

decisions.choice: much more: an argument from the greater to the lesser
decisions.reason: If God has already done the harder thing, declaring sinners righteous at the cost of his Son's blood, then he will surely do the rest. Paul uses the same argument in verses 10, 15 and 17.

decisions.choice: God's wrath (B); God's anger (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose wrath it is. Readable uses "anger", as in 1:18.

decisions.choice: shed his blood for us
decisions.reason: Readable says what "by his blood" refers to: Christ's death for us.

decisions.choice: ghadhabu (L, B); hasira (R)
decisions.reason: "Ghadhabu" is the word for God's wrath settled at 1:18. Readable uses the everyday "hasira", as the English Readable says "anger".

decisions.choice: "la colère de Dieu" (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "anger" for "wrath"; French "colère" already serves for both, so Readable keeps the same word as Balanced.

decisions.choice: "Huống chi" (L) for "much more" (also verses 10, 15 and 17)
decisions.reason: "Huống chi" is the Vietnamese way to argue from the greater to the lesser (m3). Balanced and Readable say "chắc chắn hơn", how much more certain, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 진노" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:18: "진노" at every level, Readable included, where the English Readable says "anger".

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἐχθροὶ ὄντες κατηλλάγημεν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, πολλῷ μᾶλλον καταλλαγέντες σωθησόμεθα ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: If for enemies being we were reconciled to the God through the death of the Son of him, by much more having been reconciled we will be saved by the life of him;

en.L: For if, being enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, much more, having been reconciled, we will be saved by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life.
en.B: We were enemies of God when the death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son reconciled us to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Now that we are reconciled, it is all the more certain that we will be saved by the Son's life.
en.R: We were God's enemies. But God made us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} friends again through the death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. Now that we are God's friends, we can be even more sure that the Son, who is alive, will save us.

es.L: Porque si, cuando éramos enemigos, fuimos reconciliados con Dios mediante la muerte de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, con mucha más razón, ya reconciliados, seremos salvos por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida.
es.B: Éramos enemigos de Dios cuando la muerte de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo nos reconcilió con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Ahora que estamos reconciliados, es todavía más seguro que seremos salvos por la vida del Hijo.
es.R: Éramos enemigos de Dios. Pero Dios volvió a hacernos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} amigos por medio de la muerte de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo. Ahora que somos amigos de Dios, podemos estar aún más seguros de que el Hijo, que está vivo, nos salvará.

sw.L: Kwa maana kama tulipatanishwa na Mungu kupitia kifo cha Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} tulipokuwa bado maadui, basi zaidi sana sisi tuliokwisha kupatanishwa tutaokolewa kwa uzima {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Tulikuwa maadui wa Mungu wakati kifo cha Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kilipotupatanisha naye. Sasa kwa kuwa tumepatanishwa, ni hakika zaidi kwamba tutaokolewa kwa uzima wa Mwana.
sw.R: Tulikuwa maadui wa Mungu. Lakini Mungu alitufanya kuwa marafiki {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} tena kupitia kifo cha Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Sasa kwa kuwa sisi ni marafiki wa Mungu, tunaweza kuwa na uhakika zaidi kwamba Mwana, ambaye yu hai, atatuokoa.

fr.L: Car si, alors que nous étions ennemis, nous avons été réconciliés avec Dieu par la mort de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, bien plus, une fois réconciliés, nous serons sauvés par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie.
fr.B: Nous étions ennemis de Dieu quand la mort de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils nous a réconciliés avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Maintenant que nous sommes réconciliés, il est d’autant plus certain que nous serons sauvés par la vie du Fils.
fr.R: Nous étions les ennemis de Dieu. Mais Dieu a fait de nous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} amis par la mort de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils. Maintenant que nous sommes les amis de Dieu, nous pouvons être encore plus sûrs que le Fils, qui est vivant, nous sauvera.

vi.L: Vì nếu khi còn là kẻ thù, chúng ta đã được hòa giải với Đức Chúa Trời bởi sự chết của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì huống chi đã được hòa giải rồi, chúng ta sẽ được cứu bởi sự sống của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Khi chúng ta còn là kẻ thù của Đức Chúa Trời, sự chết của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hòa giải chúng ta với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bây giờ đã được hòa giải, chắc chắn hơn nữa chúng ta sẽ được cứu bởi sự sống của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Chúng ta đã từng là kẻ thù của Đức Chúa Trời. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời đã làm cho chúng ta trở lại làm bạn với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua sự chết của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bây giờ chúng ta là bạn của Đức Chúa Trời, nên chúng ta càng có thể chắc chắn rằng Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, Đấng đang sống, sẽ cứu chúng ta.

ko.L: 우리가 원수였을 때에 그분의 아들의 죽음을 통하여 하나님과 화해되었다면, 화해된 우리가 더욱더 그분의 생명으로 구원받을 것입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 하나님의 원수였을 때 그분의 아들의 죽음이 우리를 하나님과 화해하게 했습니다. 이제 화해하게 되었으니, 그 아들의 생명으로 우리가 구원받을 것은 더욱 확실합니다.
ko.R: 우리는 하나님의 원수였습니다. 그러나 하나님께서는 그분의 아들의 죽음을 통해 우리를 다시 그분의 친구가 되게 하셨습니다. 이제 우리는 하나님의 친구가 되었으니, 살아 계신 아들께서 우리를 구원하실 것을 더욱 확신할 수 있습니다.

decisions.choice: enemies: hostile to God and under his displeasure
decisions.reason: echthros can be active (hostile to God, 8:7) or passive (treated by God as an enemy, 11:28). Both are true of people in their sin; reconciliation ends the hostility on both sides, though God is the one who acts.

decisions.choice: reconciled: brought from hostility into friendship
decisions.reason: katallassō is to change enmity into friendship. In Paul, God is always the one who reconciles and people are reconciled to him (2 Corinthians 5:18-20).

decisions.choice: by his life: by the risen life of the Son
alternatives: in his life: by sharing his life
decisions.reason: The Son who died now lives (6:9-10, 8:34); his life secures the final salvation of those reconciled by his death. en can mean "by" or "in" (sharing his life); both point to the living Christ.

decisions.choice: made us his friends again; God's friends
decisions.reason: Readable says what "reconcile" means, as 11:15 does. Literal and Balanced keep "reconcile".

decisions.choice: the Son's life (B); the Son, who is alive (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that "his" refers to the Son, and Readable that his life is his risen life.

decisions.choice: reconciliar (L, B); volvió a hacernos sus amigos (R)
decisions.reason: "Reconciliar" and "reconciliación" (verse 11) are the words 11:15 uses. Readable says what the meaning decision describes, a move from hostility into friendship, as 11:15 Readable does.

decisions.choice: kupatanishwa (L, B); alitufanya kuwa marafiki wake tena (R)
decisions.reason: "Kupatanisha" belongs with "upatanisho" (verse 11 and 11:15). Readable speaks of friendship, as 11:15 Readable does.

decisions.choice: tulipokuwa bado maadui placed after the main clause (L)
decisions.reason: Swahili cannot open with the Greek participle phrase as smoothly as English; Literal keeps every element but places "while we were enemies" after the verb it qualifies.

decisions.choice: "hòa giải" (L, B) (also verse 11)
decisions.reason: "Hòa giải" is to bring enemies into friendship (m2), and is the word the Vietnamese Colossians uses (1:22). Readable says it with the picture of friends, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "화해되다" (L); "화해하게 되다" (B); "친구가 되게 하다" (R), here and in verse 11
decisions.reason: As in the Korean of Colossians 1:20-22, "화해" is the plain current word for turning enmity into friendship; "화목" is older church language. Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

source.text: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ οὗ νῦν τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἐλάβομεν.

records.literal_gloss: Not only and, but also boasting in the God through the Lord of us Jesus Christ, through whom now the reconciliation we received.

en.L: And not only [that], but [we are] also boasting in God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
en.B: More than that, we boast in God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} this reconciliation is now ours.
en.R: And that is not all. We rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, God has now brought us back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} friends.

es.L: Y no solo [eso], sino que también [estamos] gloriándonos en Dios por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, por medio de quien ahora hemos recibido la reconciliación.
es.B: Más aún, nos gloriamos en Dios por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} esta reconciliación es ahora nuestra.
es.R: Y eso no es todo. Nos alegramos en Dios por medio de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, Dios nos ha recibido de nuevo como {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} amigos.

sw.L: Na si [hilo] tu, bali pia tukijivunia katika Mungu kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ambaye kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} sasa tumeupokea upatanisho.
sw.B: Zaidi ya hayo, tunajivunia Mungu kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} upatanisho huu sasa ni wetu.
sw.R: Na si hayo tu. Tunafurahi katika Mungu kupitia Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, sasa Mungu ametupokea tena kama marafiki {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

fr.L: Et non seulement [cela], mais nous nous glorifions aussi en Dieu par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, par qui nous avons maintenant reçu la réconciliation.
fr.B: Bien plus, nous nous glorifions en Dieu par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, cette réconciliation est maintenant à nous.
fr.R: Et ce n’est pas tout. Nous nous réjouissons en Dieu par notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, nous sommes maintenant revenus vers Dieu, et Dieu a fait de nous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} amis.

vi.L: Không những thế, nhưng [chúng ta] cũng khoe mình trong Đức Chúa Trời qua Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà bây giờ chúng ta đã nhận được sự hòa giải.
vi.B: Hơn thế nữa, chúng ta tự hào trong Đức Chúa Trời qua Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà giờ đây chúng ta đã nhận được sự hòa giải này.
vi.R: Không chỉ vậy. Chúng ta vui mừng trong Đức Chúa Trời qua Chúa chúng ta, Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, Đức Chúa Trời đã đem chúng ta trở về với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để làm bạn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그뿐 아니라, 우리는 또한 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통하여 하나님 안에서 자랑합니다. 그분을 통하여 우리가 이제 화해를 받았습니다.
ko.B: 그뿐 아니라, 우리는 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통해 하나님을 자랑합니다. 그분을 통해 이제 이 화해가 우리의 것이 되었습니다.
ko.R: 그것만이 아닙니다. 우리는 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 통해 하나님 안에서 기뻐합니다. 그분을 통해 하나님께서는 이제 우리를 그분께로 돌아오게 하셔서 그분의 친구로 삼으셨습니다.

decisions.choice: boasting: a participle with the force of a main verb
decisions.reason: Paul continues with a participle, "boasting", where a main verb is expected. It carries on the thought of verse 10: not only will we be saved, but we boast in God now.

decisions.choice: boasting in God
decisions.reason: Believers boast not in themselves or in the law (2:17, 23) but in God, as Jeremiah 9:23-24 and Psalm 34:3 (in the Hebrew numbering) call people to do.

decisions.choice: now received the reconciliation
decisions.reason: Reconciliation is something received as a gift, not achieved; "now" sets the present gift against the salvation still to come (verse 10).

decisions.choice: rejoice; brought us back to himself as his friends
decisions.reason: As in verses 2-3 and 10, and as 11:15 says "brought back to God and made friends with him".

decisions.choice: [estamos] gloriándonos
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the participle as a main verb; Literal keeps the participle and supplies the verb it needs in brackets, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: tukijivunia
decisions.reason: Swahili "-ki-" keeps the Greek participle ("while boasting") without a bracketed verb; Balanced and Readable use the plain present, as the meaning decision allows.

decisions.choice: "nous nous glorifions" (a finite verb)
decisions.reason: The Greek continues with a participle where a main verb is expected. A French participle left hanging would not be a sentence, so Literal uses the finite verb without brackets, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "자랑합니다" (a main verb) at Literal
decisions.reason: The Greek continues with a participle where a main verb is expected (meaning decision). A Korean participle left hanging would not be a sentence, so Literal uses the main verb without brackets.

source.text: Διὰ τοῦτο ὥσπερ δι’ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἡ ἁμαρτία εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθεν καὶ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος, καὶ οὕτως εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὁ θάνατος διῆλθεν ἐφ’ ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον ἄχρι γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία ἦν ἐν κόσμῳ, ἁμαρτία δὲ οὐκ ἐλλογεῖται μὴ ὄντος νόμου, ἀλλὰ ἐβασίλευσεν ὁ θάνατος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ μέχρι Μωϋσέως καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς μὴ ἁμαρτήσαντας ἐπὶ τῷ ὁμοιώματι τῆς παραβάσεως Ἀδάμ, ὅς ἐστιν τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this, just as through one man the sin into the world entered, and through the sin the death, and so to all men the death passed through, on which all sinned \v 13 until for law sin was in world, sin but not is counted not being law; \v 14 but reigned the death from Adam until Moses even over the [ones] not having sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the [one] coming.

en.L: Therefore, just as through one man sin entered into the world, and through sin death, and so death spread to all {{gender:people|men}}, because all sinned— \v 13 for until [the] law, sin was in [the] world, but sin is not counted where there is no law; \v 14 yet death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the one who was to come.
en.B: Therefore, just as through one man sin came into the world, and death came by sin, and so death reached all {{gender:people|men}} because all sinned— \v 13 for sin was already in the world before the law was given, but where there is no law, sin is not entered in the account. \v 14 Even so, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over people whose sin was not like Adam's breaking of a command. And Adam is a pattern of the one who was to come.
en.R: Sin came into the world because of one man, Adam, and sin brought death with it. So death came to everyone, because everyone sinned. \v 13 Sin was in the world even before God gave the law to Moses. But when there is no law, sin is not written down against anyone. \v 14 Still, death ruled over everyone from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. It ruled even over people who had not disobeyed a direct command of God as Adam did. Adam was a picture of someone who was going to come later: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Por tanto, así como por medio de un solo hombre el pecado entró en el mundo, y por medio del pecado la muerte, y así la muerte pasó a {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}}, porque todos pecaron— \v 13 pues hasta [la] ley, el pecado estaba en [el] mundo, pero el pecado no se toma en cuenta cuando no hay ley; \v 14 sin embargo, la muerte reinó desde Adán hasta Moisés, aun sobre los que no habían pecado a semejanza de la infracción de Adán, quien es tipo del que había de venir.
es.B: Por eso, así como por medio de un solo hombre el pecado vino al mundo, y por el pecado vino la muerte, y así la muerte alcanzó a {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}}, porque todos pecaron— \v 13 pues el pecado ya estaba en el mundo antes de que se diera la ley, pero donde no hay ley, el pecado no se anota en la cuenta. \v 14 Aun así, la muerte reinó desde Adán hasta Moisés, incluso sobre aquellos cuyo pecado no fue como el de Adán, que quebrantó un mandato. Y Adán es un modelo del que había de venir.
es.R: El pecado entró en el mundo por causa de un hombre, Adán, y el pecado trajo consigo la muerte. Así la muerte llegó a todos, porque todos pecaron. \v 13 El pecado estaba en el mundo aun antes de que Dios diera la ley a Moisés. Pero cuando no hay ley, el pecado no se apunta en contra de nadie. \v 14 Aun así, la muerte gobernó sobre todos desde el tiempo de Adán hasta el tiempo de Moisés. Gobernó incluso sobre los que no habían desobedecido una orden directa de Dios, como lo hizo Adán. Adán era una figura de alguien que iba a venir después: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, kama vile dhambi iliingia ulimwenguni kupitia mtu mmoja, na kifo kupitia dhambi, na hivyo kifo kikaenea kwa watu wote, kwa kuwa wote walitenda dhambi— \v 13 kwa maana mpaka [ilipotolewa] sheria, dhambi ilikuwako ulimwenguni, lakini dhambi haiandikwi katika hesabu mahali pasipo na sheria; \v 14 hata hivyo kifo kilitawala tangu Adamu mpaka Musa, hata juu ya wale ambao hawakutenda dhambi kwa namna ya ukiukaji wa Adamu, ambaye ni kielelezo cha yule ambaye angekuja.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, kama vile dhambi ilivyoingia ulimwenguni kupitia mtu mmoja, na kifo kikaja kwa sababu ya dhambi, na hivyo kifo kikaenea kwa watu wote kwa kuwa wote walitenda dhambi— \v 13 kwa maana dhambi ilikuwa tayari ulimwenguni kabla sheria haijatolewa, lakini mahali pasipo na sheria, dhambi haiandikwi katika hesabu. \v 14 Hata hivyo, kifo kilitawala tangu Adamu mpaka Musa, hata juu ya watu ambao dhambi yao haikuwa kama ya Adamu, aliyevunja agizo. Naye Adamu ni kielelezo cha yule ambaye angekuja.
sw.R: Dhambi iliingia ulimwenguni kwa sababu ya mtu mmoja, Adamu, nayo dhambi ikaleta kifo. Kwa hiyo kifo kilikuja kwa kila mtu, kwa sababu kila mtu alitenda dhambi. \v 13 Dhambi ilikuwako ulimwenguni hata kabla Mungu hajampa Musa sheria. Lakini pasipo sheria, dhambi haiandikwi dhidi ya mtu yeyote. \v 14 Hata hivyo, kifo kilitawala juu ya kila mtu tangu wakati wa Adamu mpaka wakati wa Musa. Kilitawala hata juu ya watu ambao hawakuasi agizo la wazi la Mungu kama Adamu alivyofanya. Adamu alikuwa picha ya mtu ambaye angekuja baadaye: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, de même que par un seul homme le péché est entré dans le monde, et par le péché la mort, et qu’ainsi la mort est passée à {{gender:tous les êtres humains|tous les hommes}}, parce que tous ont péché — \v 13 car jusqu’à [la] Loi, le péché était dans [le] monde, mais le péché n’est pas porté en compte quand il n’y a pas de loi ; \v 14 pourtant la mort a régné depuis Adam jusqu’à Moïse, même sur ceux qui n’avaient pas péché à la ressemblance de la transgression d’Adam, qui est la figure de celui qui devait venir.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi, de même que par un seul homme le péché est entré dans le monde, et par le péché la mort, et qu’ainsi la mort a atteint {{gender:tous les êtres humains|tous les hommes}}, parce que tous ont péché — \v 13 car le péché était déjà dans le monde avant que la Loi soit donnée, mais là où il n’y a pas de loi, le péché n’est pas inscrit au compte. \v 14 Pourtant, la mort a régné depuis Adam jusqu’à Moïse, même sur ceux dont le péché n’était pas, comme celui d’Adam, la violation d’un commandement. Et Adam est la figure de celui qui devait venir.
fr.R: Le péché est entré dans le monde à cause d’un seul homme, Adam, et le péché a amené la mort avec lui. Ainsi, la mort est venue sur tout le monde, parce que tout le monde a péché. \v 13 Le péché était dans le monde même avant que Dieu donne la Loi à Moïse. Mais quand il n’y a pas de loi, le péché n’est inscrit au compte de personne. \v 14 Pourtant, la mort a régné sur tout le monde depuis l’époque d’Adam jusqu’à celle de Moïse. Elle a régné même sur ceux qui n’avaient pas désobéi, comme Adam, à un ordre précis de Dieu. Adam était une image de quelqu’un qui devait venir plus tard : {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

vi.L: Vì vậy, như bởi một người mà tội lỗi đã vào thế gian, và bởi tội lỗi mà có sự chết, và như thế sự chết đã lan đến mọi người, vì mọi người đều đã phạm tội— \v 13 vì cho đến [khi có] luật pháp, tội lỗi đã có trong thế gian, nhưng tội lỗi không bị ghi sổ khi không có luật pháp; \v 14 thế nhưng sự chết đã cai trị từ A-đam đến Môi-se, ngay cả trên những người không phạm tội giống như sự phạm luật của A-đam, là hình bóng của Đấng sẽ đến.
vi.B: Vì vậy, như tội lỗi đã vào thế gian bởi một người, và sự chết đến bởi tội lỗi, và như thế sự chết đã đến với mọi người, vì mọi người đều đã phạm tội— \v 13 vì trước khi luật pháp được ban, tội lỗi đã có trong thế gian rồi, nhưng khi không có luật pháp thì tội lỗi không bị ghi vào sổ. \v 14 Dù vậy, sự chết vẫn cai trị từ A-đam đến Môi-se, ngay cả trên những người mà tội của họ không giống như việc A-đam phạm một mệnh lệnh. Và A-đam là hình bóng của Đấng sẽ đến.
vi.R: Tội lỗi đã vào thế gian bởi một người, là A-đam, và tội lỗi đem sự chết đến cùng với nó. Vì vậy sự chết đã đến với mọi người, vì mọi người đều đã phạm tội. \v 13 Tội lỗi đã có trong thế gian ngay cả trước khi Đức Chúa Trời ban luật pháp cho Môi-se. Nhưng khi không có luật pháp, tội lỗi không bị ghi lại để buộc tội ai. \v 14 Dù vậy, sự chết vẫn cai trị mọi người từ thời A-đam đến thời Môi-se. Sự chết cai trị ngay cả những người không vâng theo một mệnh lệnh trực tiếp của Đức Chúa Trời như A-đam đã làm. A-đam là hình ảnh của một Đấng sẽ đến sau này, là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.

ko.L: 그러므로 한 사람을 통하여 죄가 세상에 들어왔고 죄를 통하여 죽음이 [들어왔으며], 이와 같이 모든 사람이 죄를 지었으므로 죽음이 모든 사람에게 퍼진 것과 같이— \v 13 율법이 [있기] 전에도 죄가 세상에 있었으나, 율법이 없을 때에는 죄가 [죄로] 여겨지지 않습니다. \v 14 그러나 아담부터 모세까지, 아담의 범법과 같은 모양으로 죄를 짓지 않은 사람들 위에도 죽음이 왕 노릇 했습니다. 아담은 오실 분의 모형입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 한 사람을 통해 죄가 세상에 들어왔고 죄로 말미암아 죽음이 들어왔으며, 그렇게 모든 사람이 죄를 지었으므로 죽음이 모든 사람에게 이르게 된 것처럼— \v 13 율법이 주어지기 전에도 죄는 이미 세상에 있었습니다. 그러나 율법이 없는 곳에서는 죄가 장부에 기록되지 않습니다. \v 14 그런데도 아담부터 모세까지 죽음이 왕처럼 다스렸습니다. 아담처럼 명령을 어겨서 죄를 짓지 않은 사람들까지도 다스렸습니다. 아담은 장차 오실 분의 모형입니다.
ko.R: 죄는 한 사람, 곧 아담 때문에 세상에 들어왔고, 죄는 죽음을 함께 데리고 왔습니다. 그래서 모든 사람이 죄를 지었기 때문에 죽음이 모든 사람에게 왔습니다. \v 13 하나님께서 모세에게 율법을 주시기 전에도 죄는 세상에 있었습니다. 그러나 율법이 없을 때에는 죄가 누구의 장부에도 적히지 않습니다. \v 14 그런데도 아담 때부터 모세 때까지 죽음이 모든 사람을 다스렸습니다. 아담처럼 하나님의 분명한 명령을 어기지 않은 사람들까지도 죽음이 다스렸습니다. 아담은 나중에 오실 분, 곧 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 미리 보여 주는 사람이었습니다.

decisions.choice: "just as" is left unfinished: Paul breaks off and completes the comparison in verse 18
alternatives: the comparison is completed within verse 12: "and so death spread to all"
decisions.reason: Paul begins a comparison, "just as through one man ...", but stops at the end of verse 12 to explain how sin and death worked before the law. The "so also" half comes in verses 18-19. The SBLGNT marks the break with a dash.

decisions.choice: because all sinned
alternatives: with the result that all sinned
on the basis of which (death) all sinned
decisions.reason: eph' hō is most likely "because", as in 2 Corinthians 5:4 and Philippians 3:12. Death came to all because all sinned. How the sin of all is related to Adam's sin Paul explains in verses 18-19: through one man's disobedience the many were made sinners. The Latin translation read the words "in whom" (in Adam all sinned), which shaped later teaching on original sin; the Greek does not say "in whom" without strain, since the nearest masculine noun is far back.

decisions.choice: sin and death as powers that enter and rule
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of sin and death as if they were rulers who entered the world and took control ("death reigned", verses 14 and 17; "sin reigned", verse 21; 6:12-14). Death here is both bodily death and separation from God, the opposite of the life of verses 17-21.

decisions.choice: sin is not counted where there is no law
decisions.reason: Without a written law, sin is not entered in the account as the breaking of a known command (4:15, "where there is no law there is no transgression"). Yet people died, which shows that sin was there and was deadly before Moses.

decisions.choice: not like Adam's transgression: not breaking a direct command
decisions.reason: Adam broke a spoken command of God (Genesis 2:17). People between Adam and Moses sinned, but not by breaking a command given to them in words. parabasis is the overstepping of a stated command.

decisions.choice: a type of the one who was to come: a pattern pointing to Christ
alternatives: "what was to come": the coming age
decisions.reason: typos is a mark or pattern that something else matches. Adam's act affected all who belong to him; Christ's act affects all who belong to him (1 Corinthians 15:22, 45). "The one who was to come" is Christ, from Adam's point of view.

decisions.choice: one man: Adam
decisions.reason: The one man is Adam, named in verse 14, as the story of Genesis 3 tells it.

decisions.choice: the dash after "sinned"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Paul's broken-off sentence, with the dash, so the reader can see that the comparison is completed later. Readable writes plain statements.

decisions.choice: all {{gender:people|men}}; everyone (R)
decisions.reason: "All people" means all human beings, so the gender setting applies. Readable says "everyone", which needs no setting. "One man" is Adam and has no setting.

decisions.choice: Adam; God gave the law to Moses; the Messiah
decisions.reason: Readable names the one man, says which law is meant (verse 14 names Moses), and says who "the one who was to come" is, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: entered in the account (B); written down against anyone (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a bookkeeping word, as in Philemon 18, "charge it to my account". Literal says "counted", as for the related verb in chapter 4.

decisions.choice: a {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}}
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the English setting, as 12:17 does. "Todas las personas" is the default; the traditional option reads "todos los hombres". Readable says "todos", as the English Readable says "everyone". The same span stands twice in verse 18.

decisions.choice: la infracción de Adán (L); quebrantó un mandato (B)
decisions.reason: This chapter uses "transgresión" for a different word, the trespass of verses 15-20 (as 11:11-12). "Infracción" keeps this one apart and says what the meaning decision describes: breaking a direct command.

decisions.choice: watu wote, no setting
decisions.reason: As at 12:17: "watu" already means people of both sexes, and "wanaume" would mean males only and change the meaning, so Swahili has no gender span where the English has one. The same holds in verse 18.

decisions.choice: kifo
decisions.reason: "Kifo" (as 1:32) is used for death throughout the chapter, where death reigns as a power. "Mauti" is the older word, now mostly literary.

decisions.choice: ukiukaji wa Adamu
decisions.reason: "Kosa" is kept for the trespass of verses 15-20 (as 11:11-12). This word is the breaking of a command, and 2:23 renders it with the same verb ("kuikiuka sheria").

decisions.choice: "la Loi" with a capital for the law of Moses; "pas de loi" in lower case for the general rule (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: French Bibles mark the law given through Moses with a capital, as the French guide does. Where Paul states a general rule ("where there is no law") or speaks of a law in a wider sense (7:21-23, 8:2), the word stays in lower case.

decisions.choice: "la figure"
decisions.reason: "Figure" is the French word for a person or event that prefigures another. "Type" in this sense is a specialist word; Readable says "une image".

decisions.choice: "mọi người" (L, B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mọi người" includes men and women; Vietnamese has no traditional masculine form for the setting to offer, here and in verse 18.

decisions.choice: "không bị ghi sổ" (L), "không bị ghi vào sổ" (B), "không bị ghi lại để buộc tội ai" (R)
decisions.reason: This is a different Greek verb from the "kể" of chapter 4: a debt written into an account book (m4). Vietnamese keeps the picture of the account book and keeps "kể" for the other verb.

decisions.choice: "hình bóng" (L, B); "hình ảnh" (R)
decisions.reason: "Hình bóng" is the church word for a figure that foreshadows what is to come (m6), as a shadow goes before the one who casts it. Readable says "picture", as the English Readable does, and names Christ.

decisions.choice: Literal and Balanced end verse 12 with "... 것과 같이—" / "... 것처럼—" and a dash
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says Paul breaks off the comparison and completes it in verse 18. Korean puts "just as" at the end of its clause, so the clause can stand open before the dash, as the Greek and the English leave it; Readable writes plain statements, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "왕 노릇 하다" (L); "왕처럼 다스리다" (B); "다스리다" (R) for reign, here and in verses 17 and 21; "모형" (L, B) for type
decisions.reason: Paul pictures sin and death as rulers (meaning decision), so Literal keeps the picture of a king, Balanced says it in current words, and Readable says "rule". "모형" is the plain word for a pattern that something else matches; "예표" is a specialist church word, and Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: "여겨지지 않습니다" (L); "장부에 기록되지 않습니다" (B); "누구의 장부에도 적히지 않습니다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a bookkeeping word (English decision). Literal uses "여기다", the word of chapter 4; Balanced and Readable keep the picture of an account book.

source.text: Ἀλλ’ οὐχ ὡς τὸ παράπτωμα, οὕτως καὶ τὸ χάρισμα· εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι οἱ πολλοὶ ἀπέθανον, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἡ δωρεὰ ἐν χάριτι τῇ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τοὺς πολλοὺς ἐπερίσσευσεν.

records.literal_gloss: But not as the trespass, so also the free gift; if for by the of the one trespass the many died, by much more the grace of the God and the gift in grace the [one] of the one man Jesus Christ to the many abounded.

en.L: But not as the trespass, so also the free gift [is]. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} overflow to the many.
en.B: But the trespass and the free gift are not alike. If many died because of one man's trespass, then far more has God's grace overflowed to the many, together with the gift given by the grace of the one man Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: But God's gift is not like Adam's sin. Many people died because one man sinned. But God's grace has overflowed to many people even more. So has the gift that comes by the grace of one man, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Pero no como la transgresión, así también [es] el don gratuito. Porque si por la transgresión del uno murieron los muchos, mucho más se desbordaron hacia los muchos la gracia de Dios y el don que [viene] en la gracia del único hombre, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Pero la transgresión y el don gratuito no son iguales. Si muchos murieron por la transgresión de un solo hombre, mucho más se ha desbordado hacia los muchos la gracia de Dios, junto con el don dado por la gracia del único hombre, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Pero el regalo de Dios no es como el pecado de Adán. Muchas personas murieron porque un solo hombre pecó. Pero la gracia de Dios se ha desbordado aún más sobre muchas personas. Y también el regalo que viene por la gracia de un solo hombre, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Lakini si kama kosa, ndivyo ilivyo pia karama ya bure. Kwa maana ikiwa wale wengi walikufa kwa kosa la yule mmoja, zaidi sana neema ya Mungu, pamoja na zawadi iliyo katika neema ya yule mtu mmoja, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, imewafurikia wale wengi.
sw.B: Lakini lile kosa na karama ya bure havifanani. Ikiwa wengi walikufa kwa sababu ya kosa la mtu mmoja, basi zaidi sana neema ya Mungu imewafurikia wale wengi, pamoja na zawadi iliyotolewa kwa neema ya mtu yule mmoja, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Lakini zawadi ya Mungu haifanani na dhambi ya Adamu. Watu wengi walikufa kwa sababu mtu mmoja alitenda dhambi. Lakini neema ya Mungu imewafurikia watu wengi hata zaidi. Vivyo hivyo zawadi inayokuja kwa neema ya mtu mmoja, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

fr.L: Mais il n’en va pas du don gratuit comme de la faute. Car si, par la faute d’un seul, la multitude est morte, à bien plus forte raison la grâce de Dieu et le don [accordé] dans la grâce d’un seul homme, Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, ont-ils abondé pour la multitude.
fr.B: Mais la faute et le don gratuit ne sont pas semblables. Si la multitude est morte à cause de la faute d’un seul homme, la grâce de Dieu a débordé bien davantage sur la multitude, avec le don accordé par la grâce d’un seul homme, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Mais le don de Dieu n’est pas comme le péché d’Adam. Beaucoup de gens sont morts parce qu’un seul homme a péché. Mais la grâce de Dieu a débordé encore plus sur beaucoup de gens. Et le don qui vient par la grâce d’un seul homme, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, a débordé lui aussi.

vi.L: Nhưng ân tứ không giống như sự vi phạm. Vì nếu bởi sự vi phạm của một người mà số đông đã chết, thì huống chi ân điển của Đức Chúa Trời và món quà trong ân điển của một người là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} càng dư dật cho số đông.
vi.B: Nhưng sự vi phạm và ân tứ không giống nhau. Nếu số đông đã chết vì sự vi phạm của một người, thì ân điển của Đức Chúa Trời càng tuôn tràn dồi dào hơn biết bao cho số đông, cùng với món quà được ban bởi ân điển của một người là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Nhưng món quà của Đức Chúa Trời không giống như tội của A-đam. Nhiều người đã chết vì một người phạm tội. Nhưng ân điển của Đức Chúa Trời còn tuôn tràn cho nhiều người hơn thế nữa. Món quà đến bởi ân điển của một người, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, cũng vậy.

ko.L: 그러나 은사는 범죄와 같지 않습니다. 한 사람의 범죄로 많은 사람이 죽었다면, 더욱더 하나님의 은혜와, 한 사람 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 은혜 안에서 [주어진] 선물이 많은 사람에게 넘쳤습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 범죄와 은혜의 선물은 같지 않습니다. 한 사람의 범죄 때문에 많은 사람이 죽었다면, 하나님의 은혜와, 한 사람 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 은혜로 주어진 선물은 많은 사람에게 훨씬 더 넘치도록 부어졌습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 하나님의 선물은 아담의 죄와 같지 않습니다. 한 사람이 죄를 지어서 많은 사람이 죽었습니다. 그러나 하나님의 은혜는 많은 사람에게 그보다 훨씬 더 넘치도록 주어졌습니다. 한 사람, 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 은혜로 오는 선물도 그렇습니다.

decisions.choice: trespass: a false step, a wrong act
decisions.reason: paraptōma is a falling aside, a misstep: a specific wrong act, here Adam's disobedience. It is the word of 4:25 and is used throughout verses 15-20.

decisions.choice: free gift: a gift given out of grace
decisions.reason: charisma is a gift that comes from grace (charis), here God's gift of righteousness and life in Christ (6:23). dōrea is a gift freely given (3:24 has the related adverb, "freely").

decisions.choice: the many: all who belong to each one
decisions.reason: "The many" set against "the one" is a Hebrew way of saying "all", as verse 18 shows by saying "all people". It stresses how many were affected by one person's act, without saying how every one receives the gift (verse 17 speaks of "those who receive").

decisions.choice: much more: grace is greater than the trespass
